tasks.title: Replicas for reads
tasks.statement: There are 2500 reads per second with 100 writes. An S database handles 1000 reads and is overloaded. There is no cache. Add replicas (the database's “Replicas per shard” parameter): load at most 80%, cost at most $1200 per month. Think about which is cheaper: replicas or a bigger database?
tasks.hint: Each S replica adds 1000 reads. You need 4 replicas: 2500 / 4000 = 63%. An M database with one replica gives 83%, which is not enough.

tasks.title: Automatic leader failover
tasks.statement: The database now has a replica, but when the leader fails nothing happens: writes stop until the administrator wakes up. Turn on automatic failover so that the design survives a failure of the database leader.
tasks.hint: The database has “Automatic failover” and “Replicas per shard” parameters. You need at least one replica and automatic failover turned on.

tasks.title: Replica lag
tasks.statement: Users see stale data: the replicas are lagging. Writes load the S database the most: replica lag is over 100 ms. Reduce the lag to 50 ms without switching to synchronous replication: make the database bigger so that writes take less time on it.
tasks.hint: Lag of asynchronous replicas grows with write load: on an M database with the same writes it is noticeably smaller.

tasks.title: Synchronous replication
tasks.statement: A payment service cannot lose an acknowledged write: after the leader fails, a replica must have all the data. Turn on synchronous replication so that the lag is zero, while keeping p99 at most 140 ms.
tasks.hint: The database's “Replication” parameter: “synchronous”. It adds a few milliseconds to a write. The servers must not be overloaded, otherwise p99 will grow.

tasks.title: Four nines
tasks.statement: The contract requires availability of at least 99.99%. The load balancer and servers are already redundant, but there is a single database, and it is the one dragging availability down. Add a replica and automatic failover so that the availability of the design reaches 99.99%.
tasks.hint: The availability of a single database is 99.9%. Two copies with automatic failover give about 99.9999%.

tasks.title: A replica weaker than the leader
tasks.statement: The constraint "a replica is no weaker than the leader" cannot be shown as a direct setting, but it can be checked through load: in this design the database is L with replicas, and after the leader fails the remaining replicas must carry the load. Choose the number of replicas so that the design survives a database failure with headroom: load during the failure at most 100%, in normal operation up to 70%.
tasks.hint: When one replica fails, the rest share the reads. Two L replicas: reads 12,000 / 16,000 = 75%, too much; three replicas: after losing one, two remain, giving 75% during the failure and 50% normally.
